items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: Another time I saw them with Joe Henderson and Wayne at Lennie’s on the Turnpike.

ctx.x: Well you know I saw the Coltrane quartet maybe a half dozen times. And with McCoy, Elvin and Jimmy. And one time in 1963 at the Newport Jazz Festival Roy Haynes was there, and it was funny because Count Basie was in the afternoon, Woody Herman, and Coltrane comes on, it’s dusk, and people are leaving in droves. They just weren’t ready for that type of music. But by the time Pharoah Sanders came in the group I was totally into another kind. I was listening to Miles with Wayne, and I saw that group so many times in…

Another time I saw them with Joe Henderson and Wayne at Lennie’s on the Turnpike. So but when, as I used to see Roland Kirk there and Wynton Kelly Trio and — but I never saw the group with Pharoah play. I saw Pharoah play with his group but I never saw him with John Coltrane. I wish I had.
Well that group, from your four elements, his late recordings, “Ascension” and —
